learning: Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.10, 50 mm span) gave oval progress 0.995 and s-bend/slalom max_error 0.0676/0.0608 m. The 60 mm span tests whether a wider array reduces bend excursions. Iteration 3 (60 mm, 12 mm, kp 6, base 1.5, wheel 0.12) fell to oval progress 0.275, so the result here is decisive for whether 60 mm stays in the design.
notes: Adopts the Builder's 60 mm span at 12 mm footprints with wheel_track 0.10. Controller gains are held at the iteration 7 values so that span is the only change from the best run (399.7). If oval progress falls below about 0.65, lower kp first.
rationale: The Builder's candidate keeps the iteration 7 wheel_track of 0.10 m and widens the sensor span from 50 mm to 60 mm (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) at 12 mm footprints and y 0.05. The Builder asked for this as the next geometry test because s-bend and slalom max_error stayed on the 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau across every earlier span, footprint, lead, speed and wheel_track change. I adopt the geometry as written. I keep the controller at the iteration 7 values (base_speed 1.15, kp 3.75, ki 0.21, kd 0.375, weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, last_direction), so the span is the only variable changed from the best run so far (399.7). I considered raising kp to offset a span-related drop in steering gain, but the Builder's stated rule is to lower kp if oval progress falls, not raise it, and iteration 3 (60 mm, kp 6) showed that higher gain at 60 mm did not help. Holding the gains keeps the attribution clean. Expected behaviour is that line losses stay near 1 per run and oval progress stays at or above 0.9. The s-bend and slalom excursions are the open question, and this race will show whether the wider array changes them.
